bounded_statement: Within the supplied files of this case only: the report's [selected-result] Welch two-sample t-test (t = 12.74, df = 38.51, p < 1e-06) was computed by entering all 48 heat-ramp trial rows as independent observations (24 per shore band), even though the declared independent unit is snail_id and each of the 12 snails contributes 4 repeated rows. The reported test statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value therefore overstate the effective sample size (48 rows vs 12 independent snails; df = 38.51 vs at most 10 at the snail level) and are not supported by the design. The stated mean difference of 1.800 C itself is unaffected by the pooling, and a snail-level reanalysis would still show a significant difference, but the specific reported inferential quantities are invalid.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent rather than concealing: it correctly describes the repeated-measures structure (12 snails, 4 ramps each) and explicitly states that each trial was entered as one observation, and its reading note frames the result as exactly what the trial-level test returned. This transparency does not make the trial-level inference valid, but it means the report accurately discloses the procedure it used.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: report discloses 4 ramps per snail and trial-level entry

source_refs.quoted_text:
data/input.csv holds 48 heat-ramp trials on 12 individually tagged periwinkles:
6 snails collected from the high-shore band and 6 from the low-shore band. Each
snail was ramped on 4 separate trial days, and every ramp records the body
temperature at which the snail lost its righting response (ctmax_c, in C).

The table above is the whole of the reported analysis; the shore-band contrast
is stated exactly as the trial-level test returned it.

counterevidence_considered.description: A unit-correct reanalysis does not reverse the qualitative finding: collapsing to one mean per snail gives high-band snail means of 41.0, 41.4, 40.6, 41.8, 40.2, 41.0 and low-band snail means of 39.2, 39.6, 38.8, 39.5, 38.9, 39.2 (hand-computed from the CSV), preserving the 1.800 C gap; a 6-vs-6 Welch test on these means yields roughly t = 6.8, df = 7.9, p on the order of 2e-4 - still significant. The direction and magnitude of the effect survive; only the specific reported t, df, and p are inflated by the repeated-row entry.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: snail-level Welch approx t = 6.8, df = 7.9 vs reported t = 12.74, df = 38.51

evidence.description: The data description declares snail_id as the independent-unit column and states that one row is a single heat-ramp trial on one snail on one trial day, with each snail appearing on 4 lines.
evidence.observed_value: independent unit = snail_id; 12 distinct tags, 4 rows each

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one heat-ramp trial on one tagged periwinkle on one trial day
Independent unit column: snail_id
- snail_id: tag of the individual snail (12 distinct tags, 4 lines each)
- trial_day: 1 to 4, which repeat ramp the line comes from

evidence.description: The input data contains 4 repeated rows per snail_id; e.g., HS-01 appears on four consecutive lines with four ctmax_c values.
split_by_band pools every trial row's ctmax_c into per-band lists keyed only on shore_zone, with no reference to snail_id and no per-snail aggregation.
evidence.observed_value: 24 trial values per band pooled across 6 snails x 4 repeats

evidence.description: main() passes the pooled row-level arrays straight into scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a row-independent two-sample procedure, so each snail enters the test four times.
evidence.observed_value: ttest_ind on n=24 vs n=24 trial rows from 6 vs 6 snails

evidence.description: The report's selected statistical conclusion presents the trial-level test with n=24 per band and df = 38.51, which is only attainable by counting the 48 repeated trial rows as independent; a snail-level (unit-correct) two-sample test on 6 vs 6 snails allows at most 10 degrees of freedom.
evidence.observed_value: reported: high n=24, low n=24, t = 12.74, df = 38.51, p < 1e-06

source_refs.quoted_text:
Each heat-ramp trial in the table was entered as one observation and the two
shore bands were compared with Welch's two-sample t-test (two-sided) on the
ctmax_c column.

[selected-result] Welch two-sample t-test on ctmax_c comparing high-shore with low-shore heat-ramp trials: t = 12.74, df = 38.51, p < 1e-06. High-shore snails lost righting at a mean critical thermal maximum 1.800 C above low-shore snails.

evidence.description: The repeated rows are empirically non-independent: within-snail trial values cluster tightly around each snail's own level while snails within a band differ substantially (e.g., HS-05's four trials span 40.0-40.6 C while HS-04's span 41.5-42.2 C), so between-snail variance dominates within-snail variance and the row-independence assumption of ttest_ind is violated in this dataset, not just in principle.
evidence.observed_value: high-band snail means range 40.2 to 41.8 C; typical within-snail sample variance ~0.05-0.09 vs between-snail variance ~0.32

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the pseudoreplication reading in four ways. (1) I searched workflow/analysis.py for any per-snail aggregation, mixed-model, or clustering adjustment that would make the rows exchangeable before the test; there is none - the only grouping key anywhere is shore_zone in split_by_band, and snail_id is never read after CSV parsing. (2) I checked whether the data description could authorize treating each trial as an independent unit; it cannot - it explicitly names snail_id as the independent-unit column and labels trial_day as a repeat. (3) I checked whether within-snail correlation might be negligible in this particular dataset, which would make the violation practically harmless: it is not - each snail's four values cluster tightly around a snail-specific level (e.g., HS-05 at 40.0-40.6 vs HS-04 at 41.5-42.2), with between-snail variance (~0.32 in the high band) several times the typical within-snail variance (~0.05-0.09). (4) I verified arithmetically that the reported statistics can only arise from the row-level entry: with the reported band SDs (0.59, 0.37) and n=24 per band, Welch's t = 1.8/sqrt(0.59^2/24 + 0.37^2/24) ~ 12.7 and df ~ 38.5, matching the report, whereas any snail-level analysis of 6 vs 6 units caps df at 10. All four checks failed to falsify the finding.

root_cause: split_by_band in workflow/analysis.py pools every CSV row's ctmax_c into per-band arrays keyed only on shore_zone, discarding snail_id entirely, and main() feeds these row-level arrays (n=24 each) directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure that treats each entry as an independent observation. No per-snail aggregation or clustering adjustment exists anywhere in the workflow, so each snail's four repeated, strongly correlated trials enter the row-independent test four times, inflating n from 12 to 48 and df from at most 10 to 38.51.
